title: Nazi Germany
capsule: Nazi Germany (Deutsches Reich / Großdeutsches Reich) was the German state under Adolf Hitler and the National Socialist German Workers' Party from Hitler's appointment as chancellor on 30 January 1933 to Germany's unconditional surrender on 8 May 1945. The regime abolished democratic institutions within months, pursued aggressive territorial expansion—annexing Austria in March 1938 and dismembering Czechoslovakia by 1939—and launched the Second World War with the invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939. At its greatest extent in 1942, German-controlled territory stretched from the Atlantic coast to the outskirts of Stalingrad. The regime systematically murdered six million Jews and millions of others in the Holocaust, and collapsed when Soviet forces entered Berlin and Hitler died on 30 April 1945.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is well-attested; the dataset's from year of 1936 reflects the militarized Rhineland reoccupation rather than the 1933 seizure of power, a reasonable Cliopatria attestation choice.
